Draft affirmative.label: Draft, needs approval
Draft affirmative.say: It cannot become law until Parliament approves it.

Made affirmative.label: Already law, needs approval
Made affirmative.say: It is already law, but it stops being law unless Parliament approves it within a set time.

Draft negative.label: Draft, goes ahead unless a House objects
Draft negative.say: It becomes law unless either House objects within 40 days.

Made negative.label: Already law, unless a House objects
Made negative.say: It is already law, and stays law unless either House objects within 40 days.

recent.name: Seafarers (Wages and Working Conditions) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are made under the Seafarers (Wages and Working Conditions) Act 2023.
The Act provides powers to make regulations about the remuneration and working conditions of seafarers working on certain services.
recent.plain: This law uses powers in the Seafarers (Wages and Working Conditions) Act 2023, which lets ministers make rules on pay and working conditions for seafarers working on certain services.

recent.name: Merchant Shipping (General Lighthouse Authorities) (Increase of Borrowing Limit) Order 2027
summary: Under section 215 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995, general lighthouse authorities may borrow money for certain purposes and subject to obtaining the necessary consents.
Under section 216(1) of the 1995 Act, the aggregate amount that may be outstanding in respect of the principal of any sums borrowed is limited to £100 million.
recent.plain: Lighthouse authorities are allowed to borrow money, with the total outstanding limited to £100 million. This Order is about increasing that borrowing limit.

recent.name: International Controlled Transaction Reporting Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make provision in connection with the provision of information in relation to international controlled transactions.

recent.name: Employment Tribunals (Early Conciliation: Exemptions and Rules of Procedure) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Employment Tribunals (Early Conciliation: Exemptions and Rules of Procedure) Regulations 2014 to add to the information that prospective claimants must provide to ACAS in order to comply with the requirement to contact ACAS before instituting proceedings in section 18A of the Employment Tribunals Act 1996.
These Regulations also clarify the 2014 Regulations and make further provision regarding the early conciliation procedure.
recent.department: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
recent.plain: This law changes the rules on employment tribunals. People who want to bring a claim must first contact ACAS, and this law adds to the information they have to give ACAS when they do. It also clarifies the 2014 rules and adds detail on early conciliation.

recent.name: Financial Services (Gibraltar) (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2026
recent.kind: Part of the post-Brexit tidy-up of the law
summary: These Regulations extend by 12 months the transitional arrangements under Parts 2 and 3 of the Financial Services (Gibraltar) (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 which enable specified categories of Gibraltar-based firms to provide financial services in the United Kingdom and facilitate the access by similar types of UK-based firms to Gibraltar’s financial services market.
recent.plain: This law extends by 12 months a temporary arrangement that lets certain Gibraltar-based firms provide financial services in the UK. It also helps similar UK firms to reach Gibraltar's financial services market.

recent.name: Export Control (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Export Control Order 2008 and assimilated Council Regulation (EC) No 428/2009 of 5 May 2009 setting up a Community regime for the control of exports, transfer, brokering and transit of dual-use items (Recast).
recent.department: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
recent.plain: This law changes the Export Control Order 2008 and an EU rule of 5 May 2009 that controls the export, transfer, brokering and transit of dual-use items, meaning goods that can have both civilian and military uses.

recent.name: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (Alternative Dispute Resolution) (Conferral of Functions) (Information) and (Fees) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: The Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (Alternative Dispute Resolution) (Conferral of Functions) Regulations 2026 conferred eight functions regarding the accreditation and oversight of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) providers on the Chartered Trading Standards Institute.
recent.department: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
recent.plain: An earlier set of regulations gave eight jobs to the Chartered Trading Standards Institute: approving and overseeing the providers that settle consumer disputes without going to court. This law amends the rules on information and fees connected to that role.

recent.name: Data-gathering (Ongoing Data: Interest and Payment Card Transactions) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make provision requiring persons of specified description to provide specified data to His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs on an ongoing basis.
recent.plain: This law requires certain people and organisations to give specified data to HM Revenue and Customs on an ongoing basis.

recent.name: Customs (Tariff and Miscellaneous Amendments) (No. 7) Regulations 2026
summary: Regulation 2 amends the definition of “the authorised use document” in regulation 32(2) of the Customs (Special Procedures and Outward Processing) (EU Exit) Regulations 2018 to refer to a new version of that document.

The new version of that document introduces authorised use measures to reduce the rate of import duty on nine commodity codes relating to steel goods used in the manufacture of bright bar, a precision-finished steel bar product, and wire.
recent.plain: This law updates a customs rule to point to a new version of a document that lowers import duty on nine types of steel goods. They are used to make bright bar, a precision-finished steel bar, and wire.

recent.name: Control of Asbestos (Amendment etc.) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 to introduce a requirement that the assessment of the cleanliness of the premises, where work relating to asbestos has been carried out, is undertaken by a person who is appointed independently of the person who carried out the work relating to asbestos on those premises.
recent.plain: This law changes the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012. After asbestos work is finished, the check that the premises are clean must now be done by someone appointed independently of the person who did the work.

recent.name: Contracts for Difference (Electricity Supplier Obligations) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations relate to the levy arrangements that support the Contracts for Difference scheme established under Chapter 2 of Part 2 of the Energy Act 2013.
Government funds can be paid into the scheme to reduce the amount of the levy.
These Regulations amend the Contracts for Difference (Electricity Supplier Obligations) Regulations 2014 so as to broaden the circumstances in which that can happen.
recent.department: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
recent.plain: This law changes the levy that supports the Contracts for Difference scheme. Government money can already be paid in to reduce the levy, and this law widens the circumstances in which that can happen.

recent.name: Charities (Russell-Cotes Art Gallery and Museum) Order 2026
summary: This Order gives effect to the scheme settled by the Charity Commission for England and Wales in accordance with section 73(1)(a) of the Charities Act 2011 for the administration of the charity known as “Russell-Cotes Art Gallery and Museum”.

Prior to the Order coming into force, the Charity was governed by section 57 of the Bournemouth Borough Council Act 1985 and “the Governing Documents” as defined in paragraph 1 of the Schedule to the Order.
recent.department: Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
recent.plain: This Order puts into law a scheme from the Charity Commission for England and Wales for running the Russell-Cotes Art Gallery and Museum charity. Before it, the charity was governed by a section of the Bournemouth Borough Council Act 1985 and its governing documents.

recent.name: Bus Franchising Assessment (Approved Persons) (England) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations specify types of persons as an approved person for the purposes of section 123D of and paragraph 4(7) of Schedule 9A to the Transport Act 2000.
recent.plain: This law says which types of people count as an approved person under the Transport Act 2000 for the purposes of assessing bus franchising.

recent.name: Adult Social Care Negotiating Body for England Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations create a new, independent body, the Adult Social Care Negotiating Body England under the Employment Rights Act 2025 and set out the operational framework for that body.
recent.department: Department of Health and Social Care
recent.plain: This law creates a new independent body, the Adult Social Care Negotiating Body for England, under the Employment Rights Act 2025. It also sets out how the body will operate.

recent.name: Transport Infrastructure (Fees) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make provision for prescribed public authorities to charge fees for services provided in connection with certain transport infrastructure projects.
They are made under powers inserted into the Highways Act 1980 and the Transport and Works Act 1992 by the Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025.
recent.plain: This law lets certain public authorities charge fees for services they provide on some transport infrastructure projects. It uses powers added to the Highways Act 1980 and the Transport and Works Act 1992 by the Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025.

recent.name: Transport and Works (Applications, Objections, Listed Buildings, Inquiries and Decisions Procedure) (England and Wales) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend, subject to the transitional provisions in regulation 1, the Transport and Works (Inquiries Procedure) Rules 2004, the Transport and Works (Applications and Objections Procedure) (England and Wales) Rules 2006 and the Transport and Works Applications (Listed Buildings, Conservation Areas and Ancient Monuments Procedure) Regulations 1992.
recent.plain: This law changes three sets of rules on how applications, objections and inquiries are handled under the Transport and Works system. Some transitional arrangements apply.

recent.name: Sea Fisheries (Amendment and Transitional Provision) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make amendments to assimilated law in the field of sea fisheries.
They also make a transitional provision.
recent.department: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
recent.plain: This law changes the rules on sea fishing that came from the EU and were carried over into UK law. It also includes a temporary arrangement for the changeover.

recent.name: North Somerset (Electoral Changes) Order 2026
summary: This Order makes changes to electoral arrangements for the district of North Somerset following recommendations made by the Local Government Boundary Commission for England.
This Order does not change the boundary of the district itself.
recent.department: Local Government Boundary Commission for England
recent.plain: This Order changes the electoral arrangements for North Somerset, following recommendations from the Local Government Boundary Commission for England. It does not change the boundary of the district itself.

recent.name: Herefordshire (Electoral Changes) Order 2026
summary: This Order makes changes to electoral arrangements for the district of Herefordshire following recommendations made by the Local Government Boundary Commission for England.
This Order does not change the boundary of the district itself.
recent.department: Local Government Boundary Commission for England
recent.plain: This Order changes the electoral arrangements for Herefordshire, following recommendations from the Local Government Boundary Commission for England. It does not change the boundary of the district itself.

recent.name: English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 (Consequential Amendments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Local Government Pension Scheme Regulations 2013.

The amendments are consequential on the establishment of the Local Audit Office under the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 and provide that its employees are eligible for membership of the Local Government Pension Scheme.
recent.department: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
recent.plain: This law follows on from the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026, which sets up the Local Audit Office. It makes staff of the new office eligible to join the Local Government Pension Scheme.

recent.name: Education (Student Support for Postgraduate and Lifelong Learning Provision) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
Data Protection Act 2018 (Competent Authorities) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations add the College of Policing to the list of competent authorities in Schedule 7 to the Data Protection Act 2018.
This brings the processing of personal data by the College of Policing within scope of Part 3 (law enforcement processing) of the 2018 Act.
recent.plain: This law adds the College of Policing to the list of organisations covered by the law enforcement part of the Data Protection Act 2018. The College's handling of personal data now falls under those rules.

recent.name: Darlington (Electoral Changes) Order 2026
Central Counterparties (Equivalence) (Indonesia and the People's Republic of China) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations set out the Treasury’s equivalence determinations in respect of the regulatory framework that applies to certain central counterparties (CCPs) that are established in Indonesia and the People’s Republic of China.
recent.plain: This law sets out the Treasury's decisions that the rules covering certain clearing houses, known as central counterparties, in Indonesia and the People's Republic of China are equivalent to UK rules.

recent.name: Individual Savings Account (Amendment) (No. 3) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Individual Savings Account Regulations 1998 in relation to Lifetime ISAs.
recent.plain: This law changes the Individual Savings Account Regulations 1998 as they apply to Lifetime ISAs.

recent.name: Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: This Order brings certain drugs under the control of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 in line with recommendations from the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs.
It amends Schedule 2 to the Act, under which controlled drugs are classified as Class A (Part 1), Class B (Part 2) or Class C (Part 3).
The classification of a drug affects the criminal penalties that result from offences relating to that drug.
recent.plain: This Order puts certain drugs under the control of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971, following advice from the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs. Drugs are classed as A, B or C, and the class affects the criminal penalties for offences involving them.

recent.name: Family Procedure (Amendment No. 2) Rules 2026
summary: These Rules amend the Family Procedure Rules 2010.
recent.plain: This law changes the Family Procedure Rules 2010, the rules on how family court cases are run.

recent.name: Code of Practice (Access and Unfair Practices During the Recognition and Derecognition Process) Order 2026
summary: This Order brings into effect, on 30th October 2026, the Code of Practice issued by the Secretary of State under sections 203(1) and 204(2) of the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992 on Access and Unfair Practices During the Recognition and Derecognition Process (“the Code of Practice on Access and Unfair Practices During the Recognition and Derecognition Process”), which revises and supersedes the Code of Practice on Access and Unfair Practices during Recognition and Derecognition Ballots, which came into effect on 1 October 2005.
recent.department: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
recent.plain: This Order brings into effect on 30 October 2026 a revised Code of Practice on access and unfair practices when trade unions seek recognition or derecognition at a workplace. It replaces the earlier Code of Practice that came into effect on 1 October 2005.

recent.name: AWE Pension Scheme (Transfer of Assets) Regulations 2026
summary: Chapter 3 (AWE Pension Scheme) of the Pension Schemes Act 2026 establishes a legislative framework to create a new public pension scheme for members of the AWE Pension Scheme, and to transfer the assets of the pension scheme to government.
These Regulations are made under section 116 of the 2026 Act and enable the Secretary of State to issue directions that will require the transfer of pension scheme assets to central government.
recent.plain: The Pension Schemes Act 2026 creates a new public pension scheme for members of the AWE Pension Scheme and moves the scheme's assets to government. This law lets the Secretary of State direct that the assets be transferred to central government.

recent.name: Trusts and Succession (Scotland) Act 2024 (Consequential Provisions and Modifications) (Pension Schemes) Order 2026
summary: This Order makes provision in consequence of the Trusts and Succession (Scotland) Act 2024.
The 2024 Act excludes pension schemes established under a trust.

This is because the regulation of occupational pension schemes and personal pension schemes, including the obligation of the trustees or managers of such schemes is reserved under the Scotland Act 1998.
recent.plain: This Order follows on from the Trusts and Succession (Scotland) Act 2024, which excludes pension schemes set up under a trust. That is because regulating occupational and personal pension schemes is reserved to the UK Parliament under the Scotland Act 1998.

recent.name: Securitisation (Amendment and Miscellaneous Provisions) Regulations 2026
Northern Ireland Elections (Combined Polls 2027) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations modify the application of the legislation governing elections to the Northern Ireland Assembly and local elections in Northern Ireland in order to enable polls at those elections to be taken together on 6th May 2027, if the Chief Electoral Officer directs that the polls are to be taken together.
recent.plain: This law changes the rules for Northern Ireland Assembly and local elections so that both can be held together on 6 May 2027, if the Chief Electoral Officer decides they should be.

recent.name: Electronic Communications and Wireless Telegraphy (Amendment and Saving Provision) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are made in exercise of the power conferred by regulation 5 of the Electronic Communications and Wireless Telegraphy (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019.

They replace technical standards referred to in the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 305/2013 to include Next Generation (4G/5G) eCall and make provision for existing standards to be saved until 2G networks cease operation.
recent.department: Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
recent.plain: This law replaces technical standards for eCall, the system that automatically calls emergency services after a crash, to include 4G and 5G versions. Existing standards stay in use until 2G networks close.

recent.name: Customs (Contravention of a Relevant Rule) (Maximum Penalty) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends section 26(5) of the Finance Act 2003 to increase the maximum amount which may be prescribed as a penalty for the contravention of a relevant rule under subsection (1) of that section.
The maximum penalty amount is increased from £2,500 to £10,000.
A Tax Information and Impact Note has not been prepared for this instrument as it contains no substantive changes to tax policy.
recent.plain: This Order raises the maximum penalty for breaking a customs rule from £2,500 to £10,000. No Tax Information and Impact Note was prepared because it makes no substantive change to tax policy.

recent.name: English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 (Consequential Amendments) (Precepts) (England) Regulations 2026
summary: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 amends the arrangements for the issuing of precepts by mayoral combined authorities and mayoral combined county authorities.
recent.department: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
recent.plain: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 changes how mayoral combined authorities and mayoral combined county authorities issue precepts. This law makes the changes that follow from that.

recent.name: Sentencing Act 2020 (Prison Sanctions) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations specify the prison sanctions available to be imposed by judges in Crown Courts for contempt of court by an offender following a breach of an order to attend a sentencing hearing.

They reflect the punishments that a governor can impose for an offence against discipline as mentioned in rule 55(1)(b), (e), (j) and (k) of the Prison Rules 1999 and rule 60(1)(b) and (f) of the Young Offender Institution Rules 2000.
recent.plain: This law sets out the prison sanctions that Crown Court judges can impose on an offender for contempt of court after they breach an order to attend a sentencing hearing. They reflect the punishments a prison governor can impose for breaking prison discipline.

recent.name: Marine Licensing (Notices Appeals) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Marine Licensing (Notices Appeals) Regulations 2011, which provide for appeals to be made to the First-tier Tribunal against certain notices issued under Part 4 of the Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009.
recent.department: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
recent.plain: This law changes the rules on appeals to the First-tier Tribunal against certain notices issued under the marine licensing system.

recent.name: Marine Licensing (Exempted Activities and Fees) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Marine Licensing (Exempted Activities) Order 2011 and the Marine Licensing (Application Fees) Regulations 2014.
recent.department: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
recent.plain: This law changes two sets of marine licensing rules: the list of activities that are exempt from needing a licence, and the fees charged for applications.

recent.name: Intimate Image Reports (Trusted Flagger) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations designate South West Grid for Learning Trust as a suitable person to make intimate image reports to providers of internet services and providers of internet access services.
recent.plain: This law names South West Grid for Learning Trust as a suitable body to report intimate images to internet service providers and internet access providers.

recent.name: Social Security (Persons Detained in Hospital) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations provide for disqualification from certain social security benefits of persons detained in hospital under section 37 of the Mental Health Act 1983, and corresponding Scottish legislation, following their conviction of a serious offence.
recent.plain: This law removes certain social security benefits from people detained in hospital under the Mental Health Act 1983, or the equivalent Scottish law, after they have been convicted of a serious offence.

recent.name: North-East Atlantic Fisheries Commission (Immunities and Privileges) Order 2026
North Atlantic Salmon Conservation Organization (Immunities and Privileges) Order 2026
summary: This Order gives effect to the Headquarters Agreement between the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the North Atlantic Salmon Conservation Organization (the “Agreement”) (Cmnd 9752), as amended by the Exchange of Notes amending the Headquarters Agreement (Cm 5093).
recent.plain: This Order gives legal effect to the agreement between the UK Government and the North Atlantic Salmon Conservation Organization on its headquarters, as later amended.

recent.name: Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend provision in the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 concerning activities and operations (including waste storage operations) that may be carried out in England without an environmental permit if the operator meets certain requirements and conditions (see regulations 4 and 5 of the EPR 2016).
The requirements and conditions for exemption are currently set out in Schedules 2 and 3 to the EPR 2016.
recent.department: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
recent.plain: This law changes the rules on activities, including storing waste, that can be carried out in England without an environmental permit if the operator meets certain requirements and conditions.

recent.name: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (Subscription Contracts) (Consequential Amendments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make amendments to primary and secondary legislation in consequence of the coming into force of Chapter 2 of Part 4 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 and the Consumer Subscription Contracts (Cancellation and Information) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/XXXX).
recent.department: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
recent.plain: This law makes changes to other laws that follow from the new rules on subscription contracts coming into force under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024.

recent.name: Consumer Subscription Contracts (Cancellation and Information) Regulations 2026
Code of Practice (Right of Trade Unions to Access Workplaces) Order 2026
summary: This Order appoints 30th October 2026 as the day on which the Code of Practice issued by the Secretary of State under sections 203(1)(a) and 204(2) of the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992 on the Right of Trade Unions to Access Workplaces comes into effect.
recent.department: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
recent.plain: This Order sets 30 October 2026 as the day a Code of Practice on the right of trade unions to access workplaces comes into effect.

recent.name: Authorised Investigators (Complaints and Misconduct) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations provide for the basis on which the Director General (the “Director General”) of the Independent Office for Police Conduct has oversight of complaints and other matters relating to the conduct of authorised investigators employed by the Cabinet Office and working in the Public Sector Fraud Authority.
recent.plain: This law sets out how the Director General of the Independent Office for Police Conduct oversees complaints and other matters about the conduct of authorised investigators who work for the Cabinet Office in the Public Sector Fraud Authority.

recent.name: Tribunal Procedure (Upper Tribunal) (Amendment) Rules 2026
summary: These Rules amend the Tribunal Procedure (Upper Tribunal) Rules 2008, which govern the practice and procedure to be followed in the Upper Tribunal (other than the Lands Chamber of the Upper Tribunal), to— specify that an appeal under section 168(1) of the Online Safety Act 2023 must be brought no later than 3 months after the date on which OFCOM publishes the decision being appealed; require the Upper Tribunal in immigration judicial review proceedings to seal an application after it is accepted under rule 28A(1); require the applicant in immigration judicial review proceedings to provide a copy of the sealed application to any respondent or interested party; enable an applicant in judicial review proceedings to provide a reply to an acknowledgment of service provided under rule 29; enable the Upper Tribunal to give a decision disposing of immigration judicial review proceedings other than at a hearing, and where a decision is not given at a hearing, a party may make a written application for permission to appeal, no later than 12 working days after the Upper Tribunal sent notice of its decision to that party.
recent.plain: This law changes the rules of the Upper Tribunal. An Online Safety Act appeal must be brought within 3 months of OFCOM publishing the decision. It also changes how immigration judicial review cases are handled, and gives parties 12 working days to apply to appeal.

recent.name: Scottish Administration (Offices) Order 2026
summary: This Order specifies the Clerk of the Sexual Offences Court and Deputy Clerks of the Sexual Offences Court as offices in the Scottish Administration which are not ministerial offices for the purposes of the Scotland Act 1998.
recent.plain: This Order lists the Clerk and Deputy Clerks of the Sexual Offences Court as offices in the Scottish Administration that are not ministerial offices for the purposes of the Scotland Act 1998.

recent.name: Scotland Act 1998 (Specification of Functions and Transfer of Property etc.) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Scotland Act 1998 (Specification of Functions and Transfer of Property etc.) Order 2019 to remove reference to the Scottish Ministers’ functions under section 44 of the Climate Change (Scotland) Act 2009 (asp 12), because there are no functions under section 44 that could be exercised by way of arrangements under section 93 of the Scotland Act 1998.
recent.plain: This Order removes a reference to the Scottish Ministers' functions under section 44 of the Climate Change (Scotland) Act 2009, because no functions under that section could be exercised by way of arrangements under the Scotland Act 1998.

recent.name: School Teachers' Pay and Conditions (England) Order 2026
summary: This Order makes provision for the determination of the remuneration of school teachers (within the meaning of section 122 of the Education Act 2002 ) in England and other conditions of employment of school teachers which relate to their professional duties and working time.
recent.plain: This Order sets the pay of school teachers in England, along with other conditions of employment that relate to their professional duties and working time.

recent.name: Welfare Food (Amendment) (England and Wales) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Welfare Food Regulations 1996.

The 1996 Regulations provide for a scheme (the “Nursery Milk Scheme”) which entitles children under the age of five years to one-third of a pint of milk (189ml) on any day where they are provided with childcare, by an approved childcare provider, for two hours or more.
recent.department: Department of Health and Social Care
recent.plain: This law changes the Welfare Food Regulations 1996, which set up the Nursery Milk Scheme. The scheme gives children under five one-third of a pint of milk (189ml) on any day they are in childcare with an approved provider for two hours or more.

recent.name: Port of Tyne Harbour Revision Order 2026
summary: This Order, made on the application of the Port of Tyne Authority, modernises and consolidates the statutory harbour powers which apply in relation to the Port of Tyne (‘the port’) and provides for— The updated constitution of the Authority under the provisions of Part 2 (constitution of the Authority) in articles 5 to 12.
recent.plain: This Order, made at the request of the Port of Tyne Authority, modernises and brings together the legal powers that apply to the port. It includes an updated constitution for the Authority.

recent.name: Income Tax (Pay As You Earn) (Amendment No. 3) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make amendments to the Income Tax (Pay As You Earn) Regulations 2003 to make loans and living accommodation a “specified benefit” for the purposes of Chapter 3A of the PAYE regulations and provide methods for calculating their cash equivalent or the relevant amount for the purposes of the PAYE regulations.
recent.plain: This law changes the Pay As You Earn rules so that loans and living accommodation count as a specified benefit. It also sets out how to work out their cash value for PAYE.

recent.name: First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal (Chambers) (Amendment No. 2) Order 2026
summary: The First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal (Chambers) Order 2010 organises the First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal into chambers and makes provision for the allocation of those tribunals’ functions between the chambers.
recent.plain: The First-tier Tribunal and Upper Tribunal (Chambers) Order 2010 organises these tribunals into chambers and decides which chamber handles which work. This Order amends it.

recent.name: Building (Local Authority Charges and Amendments Relating to Charging) (England) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations set out provisions in relation to charges of local authorities for or in connection with certain building related functions.
recent.department: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
recent.plain: This law sets out what charges local authorities can make for certain building-related work.

recent.name: Persistent Organic Pollutants (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are made in exercise of the power conferred by Article 15(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 June 2019 on persistent organic pollutants (recast).
recent.department: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
recent.plain: This law is made under powers in an EU regulation of 20 June 2019 on persistent organic pollutants, a group of harmful chemicals.

recent.name: Housing (Empty Dwelling Management Orders) (Prescribed Period of Time and Prescribed Requirements) (England) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: Chapter 2 of Part 4 of the Housing Act 2004 deals with the making of interim and final empty dwelling management orders (“EDMOs) which may be made by local housing authorities in respect of dwellings which are wholly unoccupied.
An interim EDMO is an order made by a local housing authority to enable it to take steps for the purpose of securing that a dwelling becomes and continues to be occupied.
recent.department: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
recent.plain: Local housing authorities can make empty dwelling management orders for homes that are wholly unoccupied. An interim order lets the authority take steps to make sure the home becomes, and stays, occupied. This Order amends the rules for these orders.

recent.name: Anti-social Behaviour (Provision of Information) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are made under section 105A of the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014, which enables the Secretary of State to make regulations placing a duty on specified authorities to provide the Secretary of State with specific information relating to anti-social behaviour.
This may include information about reports of anti-social behaviour made to the authority, and their response to anti-social behaviour.
recent.plain: This law lets the Secretary of State require certain authorities to give them information about anti-social behaviour, which may include reports they receive and how they responded.

recent.name: Northern Ireland Assembly (Minimum Period) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: By virtue of section 31 (1) of the Northern Ireland Act 1998, ordinary general elections to the Northern Ireland Assembly are held on the first Thursday in May every five years.

The predecessor Assembly must be dissolved at the start of the minimum period which ends with the date of the poll for the election and that period is determined in accordance with an Order made by the Secretary of State.
recent.plain: Northern Ireland Assembly elections are held on the first Thursday in May every five years. The old Assembly must be dissolved at the start of a minimum period before the election, and this Order, made by the Secretary of State, amends how that period is set.
